summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, chronic back pain, and a history of H. pylori gastritis was admitted with vomiting and worsening back pain after skipping insulin and taking oxycodone without relief. She presented with diabetic ketoacidosis, elevated blood pressure, and tachycardia. Initial management included IV fluids, insulin infusion, and pain control. Labs showed resolving anion gap acidosis and transient leukocytosis, likely due to DKA. Imaging revealed no acute intracranial or abdominal pathology. An endoscopy confirmed H. pylori and chronic gastritis. Her symptoms improved with insulin repletion, antiemetics, and pain management. She tolerated a regular diet without vomiting for over 24 hours and was discharged home on her prior insulin regimen with increased metoclopramide and omeprazole, advised to follow up with gastroenterology and her PCP.
problems: Diabetes with ketoacidosis, type I [juvenile type], uncontrolled
